label: Ezer

text.BHSA 1CH 4:3: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֲבִ֣י עֵיטָ֔ם יִזְרְעֶ֥אל וְיִשְׁמָ֖א וְיִדְבָּ֑שׁ וְשֵׁ֥ם אֲחֹותָ֖ם הַצְלֶלְפֹּֽונִי׃
text.KJV 1CH 4:3: And these were of the father of Etam; Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash: and the name of their sister was Hazelelponi:
text.BHSA 1CH 4:4: וּפְנוּאֵל֙ אֲבִ֣י גְדֹ֔ר וְעֵ֖זֶר אֲבִ֣י חוּשָׁ֑ה אֵ֤לֶּה בְנֵי־חוּר֙ בְּכֹ֣ור אֶפְרָ֔תָה אֲבִ֖י בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
text.KJV 1CH 4:4: And Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah, the father of Bethlehem.
text.BHSA 1CH 4:5: וּלְאַשְׁחוּר֙ אֲבִ֣י תְקֹ֔ועַ הָי֖וּ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֑ים חֶלְאָ֖ה וְנַעֲרָֽה׃
text.KJV 1CH 4:5: And Ashur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.

A.name: Ezer
family: son-of hur (Hur, supported Moses' hands during the battle against Amalek at R)

B.name: Ezer
B.line: Judahite, son of Hur, father of Hushah
family: son-of hur (Hur, supported Moses' hands during the battle against Amalek at R)

why: The Hebrew identifies Ezer as the father of Hushah among the sons of Hur. A and B state identical identifying facts, so the text cannot favor A over B; it names one person, not both.
